title: Higher direct images commute with bounded-below filtered colimits
statement:
Let $g\colon Y\to Z$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes, $A$ a sheaf of
rings on $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$, and $(K_i^\bullet)$ a filtered diagram of complexes of
$A$-modules vanishing in degrees below a fixed $a$. Then for every $q$ the natural map
$\varinjlim_iR^qg_*K_i^\bullet\to R^qg_*(\varinjlim_iK_i^\bullet)$ of sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$
is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image] with its $X=Y$, its $Y=Z$, $f=g$, and $\mathcal R=A$. The same diagram has the same common lower bound $a$, and the morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by hypothesis. The source becomes $\varinjlim_i R^qg_*K_i^\bullet$ and the target becomes $R^qg_*(\varinjlim_iK_i^\bullet)$. The cited canonical map is induced by applying $R^qg_*$ to the colimit cocone maps $K_i^\bullet\to\varinjlim_j K_j^\bullet$, exactly the natural map in the item. Thus it is an isomorphism of sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$ for every $q$.
